notes: Most checks don't discriminate: the no-skill runs read the API source and also got ESLint (swapping out Oxlint by hand), CORS handling, the 256-char limit and email validation right. The quality gap is small (100% vs 97%).
The main win is efficiency and consistency: with the skill, runs were ~41% faster (270s vs 459s) and used ~32% fewer tokens (53k vs 78k), with about a third of the tool calls (12-19 vs 35-48).

The no-skill runs diverged on CORS: 2 of 3 switched the dev server to HTTPS with @vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl (the user must accept a self-signed cert and trust the API's cert), and 1 used a Vite proxy. All the with-skill runs produce the same proxy setup, which needs no certificate steps.
Eval 2 without skill: the token is stored but never sent as an Authorization header (no API client helper for later task calls).
Eval 1 without skill: to stop its dev server it killed every node.exe running vite on the machine, which could have hit other runs. The skill tells the agent not to start a dev server at all.
Eval 3 (disabled Sign in button) shows the skill handles customisation: the agent layered the change on the template and re-ran lint and build.
